findings.title: getForLogin loses the delegate's result ordering
findings.body: The cached branch collects identity-provider IDs and then the matching models into a HashSet and returns identityProviders.stream(). HashSet iteration order is unspecified and unrelated to the JPA delegate's ordering, so callers of getForLogin that consume the stream in order (e.g. take the first matching broker) can now observe a different, unstable provider order compared with the uncached path. Preserve encounter order (e.g. LinkedHashSet / ordered list) when materialising the cached IDs.

findings.title: Login-cache update check compares an organization-aware original against a raw updated model
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is called from update() with 'original' obtained via getById(), which returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(): its isEnabled() also returns false when the linked organization is disabled. The 'updated' model is the raw caller-supplied model whose isEnabled() only reflects the IdP flag, while the JPA getForLogin query that built the cache also only checks the IdP enabled flag. For an IdP in a disabled organization that is enabled/public (so its ID is in the cached login list), an update that sets hideOnLogin/linkOnly therefore yields predicate(original)=false and predicate(updated)=false and skips invalidation, leaving the now-hidden/link-only IdP's ID in the cached login list; callers such as OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-check isEnabled, so it can still be offered on the login page. Compute the original predicate from the unwrapped stored model (or the same semantics as the JPA query) before deciding to skip invalidation.
